findings.title: [P1] Do not render errors from superseded searches
findings.body: A second call to `search()` aborts the in-flight prior request (`this.active?.abort()` at `src/search.ts:21`). Signal-aware APIs reject on abort, so the *previous* call's `await this.api.search(...)` rejects and lands in the new `catch` at `src/search.ts:26-27`, which unconditionally calls `this.renderError(error)`. The result: an expected cancellation (or any late-arriving failure) of an old query is rendered as an error, and by the interleaving of the two async calls can overwrite the state of the newer query's result. This bites exactly in the rapid-successive-search scenario the `active?.abort()` pattern exists for, and is new behavior introduced by this diff (before it, that rejection propagated to the caller rather than being rendered). Fix: capture the controller (`const controller = this.active`) and skip error rendering when `controller !== this.active` or `controller.signal.aborted`.

findings.title: [P2] Preserve the search promise's rejection behavior
findings.body: Before this change, `SearchController.search()` (an exported public method, `src/search.ts:19`) rejected when `api.search` or `render` failed. The new `catch` consumes the error with no rethrow, so once `renderError` completes the method resolves `undefined` — silently changing the method's observable failure contract, in direct contradiction of the PR's stated goal of "preserving existing contracts." External callers that `await controller.search(q)` inside `try/catch` for retries or status handling will never see a failure (the repo has no in-repo callers to break, hence P2 rather than P1). After rendering a current request's genuine error, rethrow it.
